wfNode.itemVarHint: Blank defaults to {a}; reference the current element in statements as {b}.

wfNode.timeoutHint: Per-HTTP-request timeout; each async poll request is also bound by this.
wfNode.streamHint: Treat the upstream HTTP response as this workflow request's response stream (good for LLM). At most one per graph. Can't be combined with async polling.
wfNode.asyncPollHint: When on, on HTTP 202 or body.status=pending it polls automatically until done (protocol aligned with Provisioner). Total wait is still bound by the workflow timeout (timeout_ms); increase it for long tasks.
wfNode.fromHint: Can also be provided via the SMTP_FROM env var.
wfNode.toHint: Separate multiple addresses with commas, semicolons, or newlines; supports template variables.
wfNode.bodyHint: Fill in at least one of plain text and HTML; if both, sends multipart/alternative.
wfNode.smtpProdHint: In production, leave blank and use SMTP_USERNAME / SMTP_PASSWORD.
wfNode.conditionBranches: Conditional branches (matched in order, take the first hit)
wfNode.branchOps: Supports: ==, !=, >, <, >=, <=, contains, starts_with. Each branch maps to an exit at the bottom of the node; the edge label is the branch name.
wfNode.condTrueFalse: The true branch connects from the right exit, the false branch from the left
wfNode.switchMultiHint: After switching, a hit takes the {a} branch, otherwise the {b} branch; you can keep adding custom branches.
wfNode.whileModeHint: While mode: evaluate the condition before each loop body; loop if true, exit if false.
wfNode.untilModeHint: Until mode: evaluate the condition after each loop body; exit if true (runs at least once).
wfNode.loopCondHint: Supports ==, !=, >, >=, <, <=; can reference upstream / loop-body node outputs and {tpl}.
wfNode.maxIterHint: Prevents infinite loops; on reaching the cap it forces the done exit and sets {tpl} to true.
wfNode.countModeHint: Count mode: exits automatically after a fixed number of runs; good for batch / fixed retries.
wfNode.execCountHint: Supports a number or a template reference.
wfNode.forEachModeHint: ForEach mode: iterate each array element and run the loop body in turn; reference the current element with {tpl}.
wfNode.forEachArrayHint: Must resolve to an array type.
wfNode.concurrencyHint: 1 = serial; >1 runs elements concurrently (max 8). In concurrent mode the loop body can't reference {tpl}, and inter-iteration delay is ignored.
wfNode.iterDelayHint: Waits only between rounds; good for polling or rate-limiting.
wfNode.loopBuiltins: Loop built-in variables (reference in loop-body nodes)
wfNode.loopReachedMaxDesc: Whether it exited due to exceeding the max count
wfNode.loopResultsDesc: Array of each round's last-node output (serial mode; not available for concurrent for_each)
wfNode.loopAllowFailHint: When on, an error in a loop-body node doesn't interrupt the workflow; the loop continues to the next round.
wfNode.loopEdgeHint: Edges: the bottom-left exit body enters the loop, the right exit done goes to subsequent nodes; the loop body's last node connects back to this node's left back-edge.
wfNode.transformMapHint: Key-value mapping; values support template variables
wfNode.respBodyHint: A JSON template, or a whole {tpl}. To return an image, put a base64 string in Body and set Content-Type in Headers (e.g. image/png).
wfNode.subscribeSlug: Subscribe slug (set within the workflow, appended to /events/:slug) *
wfNode.subscribeSlugHint: Whatever you fill in becomes the client address /events/'<that>'. E.g. growth-animation → /events/growth-animation.
wfNode.exampleWayUid: Example wayUid (for generating a copyable access link)
wfNode.exampleProjectId: Example projectId (for generating a copyable access link)
wfNode.recipientUserIds: Recipient user_ids (optional, push to users individually)
wfNode.recipientHint: Fill a template or list (e.g. {a}, {b}, or a JSON array); each id is pushed separately. The topic above must then contain {c} (recommended {d}) or be in the {e} format. Blank = single broadcast by topic.
wfNode.phPushData: Blank pushes the trigger data, or enter:
wfNode.pushDataHint: Blank = push trigger data; a JSON pushes that content
wfNode.enableTimeoutDisconnect: Enable auto-disconnect on timeout (unchecked = keep connection open)
wfNode.timeoutDisconnectHint: On timeout it first sends {tpl} then disconnects. E.g. 1500 = 25 min; 600 = 10 min.
wfNode.sseClientHint: Clients should prefer the public subscribe address below; the generic authenticated channel {tpl} also works.
wfNode.subAddrDesc: This address is served by this workflow's SSE push node; save and enable the workflow to subscribe. Client EventSource can't send headers, so identity is passed via the URL param wayUid.
wfNode.subWorkflowHint: Can only call enabled workflows in the same project (matched by slug, same DB preferred).
wfNode.inputJsonHint: Used as the sub-workflow's trigger_data; the sub-workflow reads it via {a}. Supports templates: {b}, {c}.
wfNode.callWfReturnHint: The return value is the sub-workflow's response node output; downstream can reference it via {tpl}. Recursion or nesting deeper than 5 levels errors.
wfNode.allowFailureHttpHint: When on, any error of this node (timeout, connection failure, URL build failure, HTTP 4xx/5xx, missing params, etc.) won't interrupt the workflow; subsequent nodes continue. Downstream can reference the error via {tpl}.
wfNode.noDropTruncate: DROP / TRUNCATE forbidden. You can also write {tpl} templates directly in SQL (auto-parameterized to prevent injection).

helpGettingStarted.whatIsThisBody: The project workspace turns PostgreSQL into a manageable backend: create tables, configure permissions, and get REST / RPC automatically. This article only covers the first steps after you've already entered a project.
helpGettingStarted.step1: Check the project home page to confirm you're in the right project.
helpGettingStarted.step2: Use the schema selector at the top of the sidebar to pick the right schema (usually `public`).
helpGettingStarted.step3: Open "Tables" to see existing tables, or use "Table Designer" to create one.
helpGettingStarted.step4: Open "REST API" to see the endpoints generated for that table.
helpGettingStarted.step5: Create a key under "Security → API Key", then use the command below to make your first call.
helpGettingStarted.tryItBody: Replace API_BASE, the db slug, schema, table name, and key with the values from your project. The full list of methods and filter parameters is on the REST API page.
helpGettingStarted.noteBody: Creating a new project happens on the workspace selection page, not here. If you lack permission, the target feature page will block you on its own — the help directory itself always stays fully visible.

helpConnectingApis.baseUrlBody: Table REST: /api/v1/'{db-slug}'/'{schema}', followed by the table name. Function RPC: /api/v1/'{db-slug}'/rpc/'{function}'. The db slug is not the project's numeric ID — use the example on the REST API page as the source of truth.
helpConnectingApis.authBody: By default, requests carry Authorization: Bearer {apiKeyPh}, and keys start with ob_. An apikey header is also supported. Logged-in users can use a JWT. If the project has a gateway-facing base URL configured, authentication is handled by the gateway, and the caller may not need to include a key at all.
helpConnectingApis.pathSseRealtime: Browser needs real-time table change updates → SSE (see the Realtime page).
helpConnectingApis.pathWebhookNotify: Notify your own HTTP service when a change happens → Webhook.
helpConnectingApis.minimalExampleBody: For RPC, change the path to /rpc/'{function}' and use POST with JSON instead. The full set of filter parameters and HTTP methods is on the REST API page — not repeated here.

helpSecurity.whatIsThisBody: "Security" determines who can enter the project, which rows they can see, which functions they can call, and how external calls are authenticated.
helpSecurity.identityRolesBody: "Roles" implement in-project RBAC. "Identity Providers" connect external logins. The member list lives under "Member Management" in Settings, not in this group.
helpSecurity.dataFunctionsBody: "RLS" uses PostgreSQL row-level security policies to restrict row visibility. "RPC ACL" controls which roles can call which functions.
helpSecurity.callEntryBody: "API Key" is issued to external systems, and keys start with ob_. "Gateway Policy" manages access control on the external domain. When going through the gateway, see "API Integration" for how callers authenticate.

helpSettings.whatIsThisBody: "Settings" are project-level configuration and don't directly change table data. Some items can only be changed by an owner / admin.
helpSettings.projectPeopleBody: "Project Info" edits the name and other basic details. "Member Management" adds people, changes roles, and removes members.
helpSettings.secretsVarsBody: "Environment Variables" are read by the workflow runtime. "Credential Management" stores external account credentials (including keys used for cloud logs); secrets are never echoed back. "Cloud Log Source" points to a credential and specifies the SLS project/Logstore, used by the Cloud Logs page in Diagnostics.
helpSettings.connectionsGatewayBody: "Database Connection" is which PostgreSQL instance this project connects to. "Gateway Domain" configures the base URL for external access through the gateway.

helpIntegrations.whatIsThisBody: "Integrations" connect the project to external systems, or push changes out. Workflow nodes reference the connections configured here.
helpIntegrations.dataSourcesBody: "Data Sources" are shared database connections within the project, used by database nodes in workflows, so you don't need to hard-code host passwords into every flow.
helpIntegrations.pushOutBody: "Webhook" makes an HTTP push to your URL when an event occurs. "Realtime" writes table changes to an SSE topic, which browsers subscribe to using EventSource. See "Usage Notes" on the Realtime page for the subscription format and fields.
helpIntegrations.externalStorageBody: "ES Proxy", "Redis", "Kafka", and "Object Storage" each register the corresponding connection for use by workflows or proxy endpoints. Create the connection here first, then select it in a workflow node.

helpDiagnostics.whatIsThisBody: "Diagnostics & Monitoring" is read-only observability: whether things are healthy right now, where a request traveled, and which SQL is slow or blocked.
helpDiagnostics.currentStateBody: "Monitoring Dashboard" shows project-level metrics and trends. Check here first, then decide whether to drill into the logs.
helpDiagnostics.threeLogsBody: "Execution Log" records workflow/task runs made by the platform. "Audit Log" records who did what in the workspace. "Cloud Logs" queries on behalf of the project's configured log source (such as Alibaba Cloud SLS), used to cross-reference x_request_id.
helpDiagnostics.statementsLocksBody: "Statement Analysis" shows SQL shapes and durations. "Slow Queries" lists statements over the threshold. "Locks & Blocking" shows who is blocking whom.

helpDatabase.whatIsThisBody: The "Database" group operates directly on PostgreSQL objects in the current project's primary connection — it is not external API documentation.
helpDatabase.structureBody: "Tables" shows data and row editing. "Table Designer" visually creates tables or changes structure. "Relationship Diagram" shows relationships between tables. "Schema Browser" browses objects by schema. "Indexes" and "Extensions" manage performance objects and PG extensions, respectively.
helpDatabase.queryWriteBody: "SQL Editor" runs arbitrary SQL. "Transaction Editor" groups multiple statements into a single transaction. Write operations are governed by your role in the project.
helpDatabase.importBackupBody: "Data Import" loads files into tables. "Backup & Restore" exports or recovers database data. Before any large operation, confirm you're connected to the intended database.

helpAutomation.whatIsThisBody: "Automation" is logic that runs on your behalf inside the database or a scheduler — different from a one-off SQL query.
helpAutomation.functionsTriggersBody: "Functions" are PostgreSQL functions that can be called via REST/RPC or triggers. "Triggers" attach to a table's INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE and run automatically when rows change.
helpAutomation.workflowsScheduledBody: "Workflows" orchestrate HTTP, database, code, and other nodes on a canvas, and can be triggered by an API call, another workflow, or a scheduled task. "Scheduled Tasks" start workflows or other supported task types on a cron schedule.
helpAutomation.sessionRulesBody: "Session Rules" inject GUC settings / connection behavior when a database session is established — useful for setting the role or search path per request. Configure the details on that page.

helpApiRpc.whatIsThisBody: Tables are automatically exposed as REST. Database functions are called via RPC. This page only covers where to look and how to try things in the workspace — the full curl examples are on the REST API page.
helpApiRpc.restApiBody: "REST API" provides read/write endpoints for tables in the current schema, filter/sort documentation, and a shareable public docs link. Don't look for the full method reference here — that page is the source of truth.
helpApiRpc.rpcCallerBody: "RPC Caller" lets you pick a function, fill in parameters, and execute it, to confirm the function can be called externally once permissions are open. It's meant for debugging, not a replacement for your application client.

sseHelp.whatIsThisBody: Once a rule is configured, whenever the database has an INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE that matches the "event pattern", the platform automatically writes that change into the topic you specified. Clients subscribe to that topic using the browser's native EventSource long-lived connection and receive pushes in real time (no polling, no need to build your own WebSocket).
sseHelp.fieldDbScope: Database / scope: selecting a specific database only matches changes in that database; selecting "all databases in this tenant" matches every database in the tenant.
sseHelp.fieldEventPattern: Event pattern: format is schema.table.action, and * wildcards are supported. Examples: public.orders.INSERT, *.*.UPDATE, *.*.* (everything).
sseHelp.fieldTopicTemplate: Target topic template: the topic to push to when matched. Placeholders are substituted from the actual event: '{database_id}' '{schema}' '{table}' '{action}'. Example: db:'{database_id}':'{schema}'.'{table}':'{action}' resolves to db:2:public.orders:INSERT for an INSERT on db=2, public.orders.
sseHelp.fieldEventName: SSE event name: the event name used by the client's addEventListener(name, ...); if left blank, the action name (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) is used.
sseHelp.subscribeIntro: Connect to /sse and pass the JWT and the topics to subscribe to as query parameters (comma-separated, trailing * wildcards supported):
sseHelp.sampleEventNameComment: event name = the rule's "SSE event name"; defaults to INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE when left blank
sseHelp.authHint: Authorization: you can only subscribe to topic prefixes you have permission for — user:'{yourUid}':* (your own), db:'{dbId}':* (you're a member of the tenant that owns that database), sys:* (platform super admins only). Subscribing to an unauthorized topic will be rejected.
sseHelp.exampleStep1: Create the rule: choose orders database, event pattern public.orders.INSERT, topic template db:'{database_id}':orders:new, event name order_created.
sseHelp.exampleStep2: When the business app inserts a row into public.orders → the platform pushes to db:2:orders:new with event name order_created.
sseHelp.exampleStep3: The frontend calls new EventSource(''/sse?token=…&topics=db:2:*'') and addEventListener(''order_created'', …) to receive it in real time.
